title: Human whole blood and plasma from healthy participants comparing VAMS optimised sample preparation methods to other conventional methods.
projectDescription: Whole blood and plasma samples from healthy volunteers were processed using our novel VAMS-optimised technique involving selective washing steps to deplete high-abundance proteins. Samples were analysed using shotgun liquid chromatography mass spectrometry with data-independent acquisition (DIA) mode to comprehensively screen the blood proteome. The VAMS-optimised method dramatically enhanced protein detection, identifying 3024 proteins from plasma samples (4-fold increase over liquid samples) and over 3496 proteins from whole blood samples (2.1-fold increase). Analysis revealed 281 differentially expressed proteins between liquid and VAMS-optimised plasma samples, with 64% upregulated in the VAMS-optimised samples, including previously suppressed low-abundance proteins such as platelet and cytoskeletal proteins. Similarly, whole blood analysis identified 928 differentially expressed proteins between conventional and VAMS-optimised methods. Our rapid and reproducible VAMS-optimised blood preparation method enabled the production of high-quality proteomic data with mean coefficients of variation below 11% from small volumes (30 µL) of complex samples that typically require extensive depletion or fractionation prior to proteomic analysis. The method proved superior to direct VAMS processing and performed comparably to commercial protein corona bead assays while offering greater flexibility across sample types.
sampleProcessingProtocol: Whole blood and plasma samples were prepared using a variety of pre-analytical processing steps such as using different anticoagulants, centrifuges, and number of centrifuge spins. For liquid samples, whole blood and plasma were lysed directly in lysis buffer. For VAMS samples, whole blood, plasma, and serum were applied to 30µL VAMS devices and dried (Mitra, Neoteryx). VAMS-direct samples were extracted directly in lysis buffer. VAMS-optimised samples were washed in LiCl and Tris, then lysis buffer. All resulting samples in lysis buffer were then reduced and alkylated with a solution containing SDC, TCEP, chloroacetamide, and TEAB. Proteins were digested with trypsin and resulting peptides were separated on a nanoLC column (75µm x 50cm) over 62.5 minute gradient. Data was collected by MS/MS using a HF-X Orbitrap system in DIA mode. Some plasma and whole blood samples were processed with ENRICH iST bead assay (Preomic) according to manufacturers instructions alongside VAMS-optimised samples. For storage experiments, VAMS were stored at various temperatures for up to 3 months after which they were processed according to the VAMS-optimised method
dataProcessingProtocol: Raw data files were processing using DIA-NN (v. 1.8). Deep learning was used to generate a new in silico spectral library from peptides provided. Fragment m/z set to 350-1650; N-terminal methionine excision enabled; In silico digest will involve cuts at K*,R*; Maximum number of missed cleavages set to 2; Peptide length set to 7-30; Precursor m/z set to 100-2000; Precursor charge set to 2-5; Cysteine carbamidomethylation enabled as a fixed modification.
